intent: Show the values of the chart point under the pointer in a floating box, rendered by its `content`.
typical_uses: The values of every series at the hovered category
The value of the one bar or point under the pointer

dont_use_when.situation: A hint for a control or any element outside a chart

mounted_in.container: a Recharts chart element (BarChart, LineChart, AreaChart, PieChart and the like)
mounted_in.note: The tooltip reads the active point from the chart element's own state; outside one it renders nothing. The chart element is the library's, not a kit component; ChartTooltipContent additionally needs ChartContainer around it.

invariants.text: Without `content` the tooltip renders the library's own default content, which reads no ChartConfig; ChartTooltipContent is the content that resolves labels and colors from the config.

The element given as `content` is cloned on every render, or rendered as a component when it is a function, with all of the tooltip's props plus the active state, index and coordinate, the payload and the label of the active point.

anti_patterns.dont: Style the tooltip box through `contentStyle`, `itemStyle` or `labelStyle` while `content` is ChartTooltipContent
anti_patterns.do_instead: Pass `className` or `labelClassName` to ChartTooltipContent; only the library's default content reads the three style props

allowEscapeViewBox.states: allowEscapeViewBox says per axis, as `{ x?, y? }` booleans, whether the tooltip may extend past the chart's box
allowEscapeViewBox.because: `AllowInDimension` is an `{ x?, y? }` object type the compiler emits no JSON type for.

animationEasing.states: animationEasing is a named easing curve, `spring`, or an easing function for the tooltip's movement
animationEasing.because: `EasingInput` mixes strings with a function, which no JSON Schema type covers.

axisId.states: axisId is the id of the axis the tooltip attaches to, a string or a number
axisId.because: `string | number` - the compiler emits one JSON type per property.

content.states: content renders the tooltip's box: an element the tooltip clones with its props, or a function of them; the kit's is ChartTooltipContent
content.because: `ReactElement | ((props) => ReactNode)` - an element or a function, which no JSON Schema type covers.

contentStyle.states: contentStyle is a style object the library's default content applies to its box; ChartTooltipContent does not read it
contentStyle.because: `CSSProperties` - an object type the compiler emits no JSON type for.

cursor.states: cursor turns the hover cursor off with `false`, or configures it with SVG attributes or a replacement element
cursor.because: `boolean | ReactElement | SVGProps<SVGElement>` mixes a boolean with an element and an object, which no JSON Schema type covers.

defaultIndex.states: defaultIndex is the data index the tooltip shows before any interaction, a number or a string
defaultIndex.because: `number | string | null` - the compiler emits one JSON type per property.

formatter.states: formatter customises each row: the tooltip passes it to its content, and the library's default content calls it with the value, name, row, index and the whole payload array and shows its return as the row's value, or a value and name pair; how ChartTooltipContent calls it is stated in its own contract
formatter.because: A function, which no JSON Schema type covers.

isAnimationActive.states: isAnimationActive turns the tooltip's movement animation on or off, or `auto` to follow the reduced-motion preference and skip it in server rendering
isAnimationActive.because: `boolean | 'auto'` - the compiler emits one JSON type per property.

itemSorter.states: itemSorter orders the rows by `dataKey`, `value`, `name` or a function of the row; the library's default content applies it, and whether another content does is up to that content - ChartTooltipContent's contract says what it does
itemSorter.because: A union of strings and a function, which no JSON Schema type covers.

itemStyle.states: itemStyle is a style object the library's default content applies to each row; ChartTooltipContent does not read it
itemStyle.because: `CSSProperties` - an object type the compiler emits no JSON type for.

labelFormatter.states: labelFormatter returns the label's content: the tooltip passes it to its content, and the library's default content calls it with the category label and the payload; how ChartTooltipContent calls it is stated in its own contract
labelFormatter.because: A function, which no JSON Schema type covers.

labelStyle.states: labelStyle is a style object the library's default content applies to the label; ChartTooltipContent does not read it
labelStyle.because: `CSSProperties` - an object type the compiler emits no JSON type for.

offset.states: offset is the gap in pixels between the pointer and the tooltip, one number or an `{ x, y }` pair
offset.because: `number | Coordinate` - the compiler emits one JSON type per property.

payloadUniqBy.states: payloadUniqBy is a boolean or a function returning each row's identity, deciding which duplicate rows the tooltip drops before its content renders
payloadUniqBy.because: `boolean | ((entry) => unknown)` - a function, which no JSON Schema type covers.

portal.states: portal is the element the tooltip renders into; without it the tooltip renders inside the chart's wrapper
portal.because: `HTMLElement | null` - a live DOM node, which no JSON Schema type covers.

position.states: position fixes the tooltip at `{ x?, y? }` pixels; an axis left out follows the pointer
position.because: `Partial<Coordinate>` - an object type the compiler emits no JSON type for.

reverseDirection.states: reverseDirection says per axis, as `{ x?, y? }` booleans, whether the tooltip opens on the opposite side of the pointer
reverseDirection.because: `AllowInDimension` is an `{ x?, y? }` object type the compiler emits no JSON type for.

wrapperStyle.states: wrapperStyle is a style object for the tooltip's positioned wrapper element
wrapperStyle.because: `CSSProperties` - an object type the compiler emits no JSON type for.

good.title: The kit's content with a line indicator
good.code:
<ChartContainer config={chartConfig}>
  <BarChart data={data}>
    <Bar dataKey="desktop" fill="var(--color-desktop)" />
    <ChartTooltip cursor={false} content={<ChartTooltipContent indicator="line" />} />
  </BarChart>
</ChartContainer>

bad.title: A tooltip outside the chart element
bad.why: The tooltip reads the active point from a chart element; with none around it, it renders nothing.
